title: A daily dose of 5 mg folic acid for 90 days is associated with increased serum unmetabolized folic acid and reduced natural killer cell cytotoxicity in healthy Brazilian adults
authors: Paniz C, Bertinato JF, Lucena MR, De Carli E, Amorim PMDS, Gomes GW, et al.
followUp: 90 days, samples at baseline, 45 and 90 days
population: Healthy Brazilian adults (15 women), mean age 27.7 years, in a country with mandatory fortification at 150 µg folic acid per 100 g flour, where the government recommends 5 mg daily to women who want to conceive or are pregnant and the 5 mg tablet is the main formulation; uncontrolled before-after trial
funder: This study was supported by Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo (FAPESP 2012/12912-1) and Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq), Brazil; fellowships from CNPq, CAPES and FAPESP.
authorConflicts: The authors have no conflicts of interest to declare.
result: Folic acid 5 mg daily raised serum folate about 5-fold; unmetabolised folic acid rose 11.9-fold at 45 days and 5.9-fold at 90 days, exceeding 1.12 nmol/L in 29 of 30 and 26 of 30 participants. The number (P < 0.001) and cytotoxicity (P = 0.003) of natural killer cells fell at 45 and 90 days; mononuclear-cell DHFR mRNA rose at 90 days and IL8 and TNFA mRNA at 45 and 90 days. The authors describe the trial as non-controlled.
